security_audit.summary: The skill is a landing page design guide, but it tells agents to run belt and npx commands. Those commands invoke external services or install related skills, which creates medium external command risk. Most other static backtick findings are Markdown formatting false positives, and no prompt injection text was found.

remediation.suggestion: Replace Bash(belt *) with a narrower allowed-tools policy or require confirmation before running nonessential belt subcommands.
Replace npx skill install examples with verified marketplace dependency metadata, or warn users to inspect packages before execution.
Disclose that prompts and search queries may be sent to inference.sh, Tavily, Exa, Fal.ai, ByteDance, and html-to-image providers.
Point to signed release documentation or a stable docs page instead of raw content from a moving branch.

content.value_statement: Landing pages often fail because message, proof, and CTA placement are unclear. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical rules for hero sections, social proof, forms, mobile layout, and AI-generated visuals.
actual_capabilities: Defines an above-the-fold formula with headline, subheadline, hero image, CTA, and social proof elements.
Provides headline and CTA rules with examples of strong and weak conversion copy.
Recommends a complete landing page section order from hero to final CTA.
Guides outcome-focused hero image prompts for external AI image generation tools.
Covers social proof, form design, mobile optimization, OG images, and page speed targets.
limitations: Image generation and research examples depend on the external belt CLI and third-party services.
The skill does not build, host, or deploy a complete landing page by itself.
Conversion advice is general and should be validated with analytics or A/B testing.
Competitive research and market claims require current verification before publication.

use_cases.title: Plan a Startup Launch Page
use_cases.description: Create a clear first-page structure with an outcome headline, primary CTA, proof section, and signup form guidance.

use_cases.title: Improve SaaS Conversion Copy
use_cases.description: Review hero messaging, CTA text, social proof placement, and pricing flow for a product marketing page.

use_cases.title: Guide Visual Direction
use_cases.description: Translate product outcomes into hero image concepts, OG image prompts, and mobile-first layout requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a First Landing Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new product page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the landing-page-design skill to outline a landing page for [product]. Include headline, subheadline, primary CTA, social proof, and section order.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Hero and CTA
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this hero section for conversion clarity: [paste copy]. Suggest a stronger headline, subheadline, CTA text, and proof placement.

prompt_templates.title: Design for Mobile Conversion
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to adapt this landing page for mobile users: [describe page]. Prioritize CTA access, form length, typography, and image behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Competitive Funnel
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my landing page goals with three competitor examples. Identify message gaps, proof gaps, risky claims, and A/B test ideas.

output_examples.input: A founder needs a landing page for an AI meeting notes product.
output: Headline: Turn every meeting into a clear action plan.
Subheadline: Capture decisions, owners, and follow-ups automatically so teams leave every meeting aligned.
Primary CTA: Start Free Trial. Social proof should appear directly below the CTA.

output_examples.input: A SaaS marketer asks why a signup page has weak conversion.
output: The hero headline is vague and does not state the user outcome.
The form asks for too much information before trust is established.
Move customer logos above the first scroll point and repeat the CTA after pricing.

output_examples.input: A designer needs hero image direction for a dashboard product.
output_examples.output: Show the outcome of using the dashboard: a team reviewing clear growth results on one screen. Avoid abstract backgrounds and hard-to-read screenshots.

best_practices: Start with one clear user outcome before choosing layout, copy, or visuals.
Place the primary CTA and strongest proof where users can see them without scrolling.
Validate claims, social proof, and conversion recommendations with current evidence.
anti_patterns: Using a vague headline that describes the company instead of the customer outcome.
Adding multiple competing CTAs before the visitor understands the offer.
Using decorative hero images that do not explain the product result.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps plan and improve landing pages with stronger hero sections, CTAs, proof, forms, mobile layout, and visuals.

faq.question: Can it generate images?
faq.answer: It includes prompts and belt CLI examples for external image tools, but image generation depends on those services.

faq.question: Does it write production code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on conversion strategy, page structure, copy guidance, and visual direction.

faq.question: Is it useful for SaaS pages?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers SaaS hero messaging, social proof, pricing flow, signup forms, and mobile conversion.

faq.question: Should teams trust every conversion claim?
faq.answer: No. Teams should validate market claims, social proof, and conversion improvements with current analytics or tests.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
